newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh army chief rules out grabbing power.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh army chief rules out grabbing power.

text.p: The army chief of Bangladesh, which has been ruled by generals for 15 of its 25 years of independent history, has ruled out grabbing power, saying his duty is to uphold democracy.

"I can't grab state power as the army chief. I am bound by pledge to preserve the constitution," army chief of staff Lieutenant-General Mahbubur Rahman was quoted as saying in Tuesday's Ajker Kagoj newspaper.
"Military law...does not permit grabbing state power. Those who did it in the past did something unlawful and undesirable. I can't act for self interest as chief of the army."
Rahman's interview coincided with a plea by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in parliament on Monday that Bangladeshis unite to help her two-month-old government promote democracy and development.
Hasina is the daughter of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, Bangladesh's independence leader who was killed along with most of his family in a military coup in 1975.
Bangladesh gained its independence from Pakistan in 1971.

Army chief Rahman was appointed in May, replacing Lieutenant-General Abu Saleh Mohammad Nasim who was sacked by President Abdur Rahman Biswas for disloyalty and attempted revolt along with several senior officers.

In the newspaper interview, he criticised a 1982 bloodless military coup in which then army chief Hossain Mohammad Ershad ousted the Bangladesh National Party government, saying this had tarnished the image of the armed forces.
"Those involved in grabbing power through illegal means must be punished," he said.
Ershad was jailed in 1990 for corruption. He joined parliament on parole after he won five seats in the June polls which returned the Awami League to power after 21 years.
